records.subagent_summary: Execution 148.156 scored 3 of 8; three failures hit the 16384-token cap and the terminating failures named a candidate they had just argued was impossible. Checking which incumbent clauses the rollouts actually execute, the trailing 'do not reason from the original set after later statements' clause appears only inside verbatim recitations of the hint - no rollout, winning or losing, ever performs it as a distinct step, and two of the three successes never mention it at all; it is redundant with 'recomputing information sets after every deletion' anyway. So this is a pure lossless compression: all four working steps (enumerate interpretations as a candidate set, group by each speaker's private value, read not-knowing as deleting size-one groups, re-filter in chronological order, survivor gives the answer) are kept word for word at 66 tokens instead of 77. Rounds 6 and 7 also dropped this clause but each added new clauses alongside; nothing has yet tested the deletion on its own.

Fresh rollouts (execution_id 148.157) scored 8/8, so nothing on train is broken and the gap is transfer. Clause-tracing all eight shows two things: every trace relaxed the finite root set to the FULL circle and took the image of that circle (8/8), the step the incumbent leaves implicit behind a bare 'image locus'; and only 2 of 8 ever mentioned an exceptional value, so 'check exceptional values' is inert text that costs transfer. This edit therefore names the move the rollouts actually make and drops the unused clause, at 69 tokens versus 70. It deliberately keeps the concrete w=(z-1)/z anchor (round 6 lost by generalizing it) and keeps the geometric-or-xy fork (round 7 lost by replacing it with a rigid procedure), and it appends no guard (rounds 2 and 4 lost that way).

Fresh rollouts scored 7/8; all eight closed the reasoning block and all eight ended on a box, and in every one the first box sits at 96-99 percent of the write-up, after a full 'To determine...' recap. So the incumbent's clause ordering the box first with explanation after it was disobeyed 8/8 here and 8/8 in round 6: it is inert text paying transfer tax on ten unseen problems. This edit deletes only that sentence and leaves every other word byte-identical, so the opening grading rule, the close-early rule, the no-restart rule, the coordinate/extent setup and the invariance and sum-minus-overlap facts that the successful traces actually execute are all preserved, while the hint drops from 169 to 137 tokens. The one failure was a method slip (overlap taken as the whole small square), which no output-protocol wording addresses.

Fresh round-8 rollouts (execution 148.159) scored 5/8. All three failures share one mechanical slip: they compute the degree of P(x)-L(x) by subtracting degrees (deg P minus 1) instead of reading its surviving leading coefficient, so the per-polynomial capacity comes out one too small and the reported total is short by one menu's worth; both truncated rollouts then oscillate on whether a high-degree polynomial must be linear and never commit. The edit is a lossless compression of the incumbent (148 vs 153 tokens, every step kept) that spends the freed words on the leading-coefficient cue and pins the capacity as deg P, never deg P minus one.

Five of eight rollouts scored. All three failures broke at one identical step: they kept the defining relation in inverse (logarithmic) form and mis-manipulated it when combining two conditions, producing a negative discriminant or a collapsed identity, then spent the rest of the budget re-litigating the setup. Every success instead converted the relation once into an inverse-free algebraic form and worked polynomially; round 7 showed the same split. So the incumbent's 'a zero or impossible intermediate means relabel, not restart' clause is replaced by that concrete first move - undo logs, roots and exponents before substituting. The clause removed is provably inert: no rollout in rounds 5-8 ever relabels. Length is unchanged at 70 tokens, and this is a positive setup instruction rather than a caution, so it should transfer to any unseen problem whose conditions hide behind an inverse operator.

Fresh rollouts scored 0/8. Part (b) failed every run in one of two ways: four priced 'this bag arrives at the destination first' as one or two isolated coin flips (1/4, 1/2), and three declared the source must drain in bottom-up order so the placement is impossible (0); two ran to the token limit re-arguing that claim. Clause-level grep of the eight rollouts shows the labeling, forced-move and arrived-first clauses are used (8/8, 6/8, 7/8) while 'sum to one', 'red flag' and 'unreachable' appear 0/8. Rounds 2-7 all tried adding or swapping content and every one lost heldout, including round 7's removal of the inert sum-to-one check and round 6's partial compression. So this round changes no strategy at all: it is a pure rewording that keeps all fourteen clauses, including the inert ones, and only removes redundant phrasing, banking the 8-token tiebreak without risking a clause the working rollouts lean on.

Fresh round-8 rollouts scored 1/8, and the derailment point is now precise: every rollout that reached a small case tried the incumbent's literal first size (2), found it degenerate/inconsistent, concluded its own setup or the shrink was wrong, and abandoned the table for Vandermonde/Vieta theory until the 16384-token cap; seven produced no boxed value. The single winner was the only rollout that carried the ladder past that size to the next two sizes and read the rule off three exact entries. So the failing clause is not the strategy but the starting number: the smallest instance of a parametrized family is usually degenerate. Starting one step up costs zero tokens (70, same as incumbent), keeps every clause the winner used, and transfers because degenerate smallest cases are common across unseen problems.

Fresh round-8 rollouts scored 7/8, and all eight executed the same machinery: gcd of the stage totals, divisors as candidate counts, percent applied to cost. The lone failure was not a missing step but a plausibility pick among already-listed candidates. History shows every attempt to patch that fork loses held-out (added tiebreak rounds 2 and 6, executable grouping filter round 7) and deleting the grouping clause cost 0.625 train in round 4, while both wins for this hint (rounds 3 and 5) were compressions. So this is a lossless compression: all seven moves the rollouts rely on are preserved verbatim in meaning, only wording is tightened (paraphrased three noun phrases), 116 tokens versus 123, no clause added or dropped.

1/8 correct; all seven failures died on the 16384-token cap. Every rollout did adopt the involution ansatz, so that wording works, but the incumbent's next clause tells them to read outputs off the relation 'rather than solving for every coefficient', which forbids the one step the single winner actually took: expand only the one-variable reflection identity to get coefficient relations, accept that one parameter stays free, and let it cancel in the requested values. Lacking that step the failures had nowhere to go, so six reverted to full composition coefficient matching and five declared a contradiction or that no such polynomials exist. The edit swaps that misdirecting clause for the concrete positive move and pre-empts the underdetermined-means-contradiction abort; it is 149 tokens versus the incumbent's 152.

Fresh rollouts under the incumbent scored 3/8. Three of the five failures never obtained a second real data point: they wrote out only the smallest case, then filled in larger sizes from an unrun structural claim and fit a formula to those invented numbers; the other two burned the cap arguing with a contradiction between their own written states and such a claim. The incumbent's 'get one more size the same way' is the inert clause here - nobody does it, because writing every state at the next size is unaffordable. I replace it with a concrete, cheap way to measure that second size: track a single label under repeated whole applications and count until it returns. This should transfer to any period/order or repeated-process question, and it holds length exactly at the incumbent's 106 tokens.
